::::::::::::::::::: {#frequently-asked-questions .section}
[]{#faq}

# Frequently Asked Questions[¶](#frequently-asked-questions "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

This is a list of Frequently Asked Questions regarding using
[`flogin`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} and its extension
modules. Feel free to suggest a new question or submit one via pull
requests.

::::::::::: {#coroutines .section}
## Coroutines[¶](#coroutines "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

Questions regarding coroutines and asyncio belong here.

::: {.admonition .note}
Note

Credits for the [`Coroutines`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}
section goes to
[discord.py](https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/faq.html?highlight=on_error#coroutines){.reference
.external}
:::

::: {#what-is-a-coroutine .section}
### What is a coroutine?[¶](#what-is-a-coroutine "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

A
[*coroutine*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine){.reference
.external} is a function that must be invoked with [`await`{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}]{.pre} or [`yield`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}[`from`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}. When
Python encounters an [`await`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} it
stops the function's execution at that point and works on other things
until it comes back to that point and finishes off its work. This allows
for your program to be doing multiple things at the same time without
using threads or complicated multiprocessing.

**If you forget to await a coroutine then the coroutine will not run.
Never forget to await a coroutine.**
:::

::: {#where-can-i-use-await .section}
### Where can I use [`await`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}?[¶](#where-can-i-use-await "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

You can only use [`await`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} inside
[`async`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}[`def`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} functions
and nowhere else.
:::

::::::: {#what-does-blocking-mean .section}
### What does "blocking" mean?[¶](#what-does-blocking-mean "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

In asynchronous programming a blocking call is essentially all the parts
of the function that are not [`await`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}. Do not despair however, because not all forms of
blocking are bad! Using blocking calls is inevitable, but you must work
to make sure that you don't excessively block functions. Remember, if
you block for too long then your bot will freeze since it has not
stopped the function's execution at that point to do other things.

A common source of blocking for too long is something like
[[`time.sleep()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.sleep "(in Python v3.14)"){.reference
.external}. Don't do that. Use [[`asyncio.sleep()`{.xref .py .py-func
.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.sleep "(in Python v3.14)"){.reference
.external} instead. Similar to this example:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    # bad
    time.sleep(10)

    # good
    await asyncio.sleep(10)
:::
::::

Another common source of blocking for too long is using HTTP requests
with the famous module [Requests: HTTP for
Humans™](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ "(in Requests v2.34.2)"){.reference
.external}. While [Requests: HTTP for
Humans™](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ "(in Requests v2.34.2)"){.reference
.external} is an amazing module for non-asynchronous programming, it is
not a good choice for [[`asyncio`{.xref .py .py-mod .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html#module-asyncio "(in Python v3.14)"){.reference
.external} because certain requests can block the event loop too long.
Instead, use the [[aiohttp]{.xref .std
.std-doc}](https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/index.html "(in aiohttp v3.14)"){.reference
.external} library which is installed on the side with this library.

Consider the following example:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    # bad
    r = requests.get('https://httpbin.org/get')
    if r.status_code == 200:
        js = r.json()
        yield Result(f"User Agent: {js['headers']['User-Agent']}")

    # good
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get('https://httpbin.org/get') as r:
            if r.status == 200:
                js = await r.json()
                yield Result(f"User Agent: {js['headers']['User-Agent']}")
:::
::::
:::::::
:::::::::::

::::::: {#general .section}
## General[¶](#general "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

General questions regarding library usage belong here.

::: {#where-can-i-find-usage-examples .section}
### Where can I find usage examples?[¶](#where-can-i-find-usage-examples "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

Example code can be found in the [examples
folder](https://github.com/cibere/flogin/tree/master/examples){.reference
.external} in the repository.

For live projects that you can use as references for "advanced" plugins,
see the following plugins:

- [FirefoxKeywordBookmarks by
  cibere](https://github.com/cibere/FirefoxKeywordBookmarks){.reference
  .external}

- [WordnikDictionary by
  cibere](https://github.com/cibere/Flow.Launcher.Plugin.WordNikDictionary){.reference
  .external} *(The development version uses flogin)*

- [Wordle by
  cibere](http://github.com/cibere/flow.launcher.plugin.wordle){.reference
  .external}
:::

::: {#where-can-i-get-help-with-using-the-library .section}
### Where can I get help with using the library?[¶](#where-can-i-get-help-with-using-the-library "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

You can ask questions in [flow's official discord
server](https://discord.gg/QDbDfUJaGH){.reference .external}
:::

::: {#how-do-highlights-work .section}
[]{#highlights}

### How do highlights work?[¶](#how-do-highlights-work "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

Highlight data works by marking which characters should be highlighted,
by including their index in a list. Take the following string as an
example: [`Hello`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}[`World`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}.
If I wanted to just highlight [`Hello`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}, the highlight data would be [`(0,`{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}[`1,`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}[`2,`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal .notranslate}[`3,`{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}[`4)`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}. If I wanted
to just highlight [`World`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}, the
highlight data would be [`(6,`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal .notranslate}[`7,`{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}[`8,`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}[`9,`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal .notranslate}[`10)`{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}]{.pre}. If I just wanted to highlight the vowels,
I would do: [`(1,`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}[`4,`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}` `{.docutils .literal .notranslate}[`7)`{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}]{.pre}.
:::

::: {#why-are-the-only-supported-python-versions-3-11-and-3-12 .section}
### Why are the only supported python versions 3.11 and 3.12?[¶](#why-are-the-only-supported-python-versions-3-11-and-3-12 "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

When a user installs a python plugin, flow prompts them to either locate
a python installation or install an embedded version of python. The
embedded version of python is 3.11. However, as the user can also
install other versions of python, 3.12 is also supported.
:::
:::::::

:::: {#flow-launcher .section}
## Flow Launcher[¶](#flow-launcher "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

Questions related to flogin and flow launcher belong here.

::: {#what-is-the-difference-between-the-v1-api-and-the-v2-api .section}
### What is the difference between the V1 API and the V2 API?[¶](#what-is-the-difference-between-the-v1-api-and-the-v2-api "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

The V1 API is partially documented, and creates a new instance of the
plugin for each query/request. However the V2 API is completely
undocumented (which is why I am trying to document flogin as much as
possible), and has a single instance for the lifespan of flow itself.
This allows for more efficient memory usage and faster response times.
:::
